title: Cameras, Radar, Lidar: How Self-Driving Cars See 👁️📡 #shorts

scenes.text: A self-driving car has three kinds of eyes. Each one is blind to something the others can see.
Cameras see like you do. They read signs, lane lines and traffic-light colors. But glare, darkness and fog hurt them, and distance must be guessed by software.
Radar sends out radio waves. The echo gives distance and speed, even in rain or fog. But it's blurry. It can't tell a deer from a rock.
Lidar fires laser pulses and times each echo. Every return becomes a dot in a precise 3D map. But fog and snow scatter the light, and it's been costly.
So most robotaxis fuse all three. Tesla is the big exception: since twenty twenty-one, it has bet on cameras alone.
Is one kind of eye ever enough? Follow EV Drive.
